name: Fixed-step gradient descent
definition: x_(k+1)=x_k−η∇f(x_k). If f is convex with L-Lipschitz gradient, an attained minimum and 0<η≤1/L, f(x_k)−f(x*)≤‖x₀−x*‖₂²/(2ηk) for k≥1.
variables: f differentiable training loss, x coefficient vector, η step, L gradient Lipschitz constant, x* minimizer
assumptions: Euclidean gradient evaluated on a fixed smooth convex objective for the stated bound
limitations: A step larger than the smoothness bound can oscillate or diverge
failure_conditions: A step larger than the smoothness bound can oscillate or diverge
computation: One full gradient evaluation and O(d) vector operations per step
application: Fit a differentiable historical calibration or margin loss by full gradient updates
required_inputs: A documented training objective built from timestamped prior inputs, or an explicitly specified synthetic objective

name: Iterative shrinkage-thresholding
definition: For F(x)=f(x)+λ‖x‖₁, set u=x_k−∇f(x_k)/L and x_(k+1),j=sign(u_j)max(abs(u_j)−λ/L,0).
variables: f smooth convex training loss, λ≥0 penalty, L>0 upper bound on the gradient Lipschitz constant, j feature index
assumptions: Fixed convex composite objective with a minimizer and valid smoothness bound
limitations: Poor curvature can slow progress and arbitrary feature scales change the L₁ fit
failure_conditions: Poor curvature can slow progress and arbitrary feature scales change the L₁ fit
computation: One gradient plus O(d) shrinkage operations per step

source.citation: Beck and Teboulle (2009), A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems, §3. https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~carlier/FISTA

name: Accelerated iterative shrinkage-thresholding
definition: Initialize y₁=x₀ and t₁=1. With soft threshold S_a(u)_j=sign(u_j)max(abs(u_j)−a,0), set x_k=S_(λ/L)(y_k−∇f(y_k)/L), t_(k+1)=(1+√(1+4t_k²))/2, and y_(k+1)=x_k+[(t_k−1)/t_(k+1)](x_k−x_(k−1)).
variables: f smooth convex loss, λ≥0 L₁ penalty, L>0 upper bound on the gradient Lipschitz constant, x fitted iterate, y extrapolated point, t acceleration scalar
assumptions: Fixed convex composite objective with a minimizer and a valid smoothness bound
limitations: Acceleration can yield nonmonotone objective values at successive fitted iterates
failure_conditions: Acceleration can yield nonmonotone objective values at successive fitted iterates
computation: One gradient plus O(d) shrinkage and extrapolation operations per step

source.citation: Beck and Teboulle (2009), A Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm for Linear Inverse Problems, §4. https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~carlier/FISTA

name: Frank–Wolfe conditional gradient
definition: At k≥0 choose s_k∈argmin_(s∈C) ⟨s,∇f(x_k)⟩ and set x_(k+1)=(1−γ_k)x_k+γ_k s_k with γ_k=2/(k+2). The gap ⟨x_k−s_k,∇f(x_k)⟩ bounds suboptimality for convex f.
variables: C compact convex feasible set, x₀∈C, s linear minimization oracle output, γ step, f differentiable loss
assumptions: A reliable linear oracle and a smooth convex objective for standard rate guarantees
limitations: A costly linear oracle or near-face zigzagging can make iterations inefficient
failure_conditions: A costly linear oracle or near-face zigzagging can make iterations inefficient
computation: One gradient and one linear oracle call per step

name: Quadratic equality-penalty continuation
definition: For equality constraints h(x)=0, solve x_c∈argmin_x [f(x)+(c/2)‖h(x)‖₂²] for increasing c→∞. With continuous f and h, feasible original problem and globally minimizing subproblems, finite accumulation points solve the original problem.
variables: f historical fit objective, h equality residual vector, c>0 penalty weight, x_c penalized optimum
assumptions: Subproblem minimizers exist and the iterates have an accumulation point for the limit claim
limitations: Large penalties can make the inner system ill-conditioned and finite-c solutions generally violate equality
failure_conditions: Large penalties can make the inner system ill-conditioned and finite-c solutions generally violate equality
computation: One penalized optimization per continuation value
